title: File Integrity Ledger — Offline Checksum Snapshot
customer_problem: People need to check whether selected local files changed or disappeared after transfer or backup, and preserve a verifiable snapshot without uploading data or modifying the files.
audience: Individual Windows users comparing a small set of documents, media, or backup files between sessions who need clear local evidence rather than an automated cleanup utility.
differentiation: Read-only SHA-256 snapshot ledger with explicit missing/modified/unchanged results, durable JSON snapshots and CSV reporting; never deletes, renames, uploads, or silently repairs source files.
scope: Choose up to 100 regular local files and calculate SHA-256 digests with bounded file sizes and explicit symlink/error handling.
Save and reopen validated JSON snapshots atomically with a recoverable previous version; retain paths, sizes and hashes for later verification.
Verify snapshots against current files, clearly reporting unchanged, modified, missing, or unreadable items without modifying source files.
Export safe CSV results for user review, including protections against spreadsheet formula injection in file names and paths.
Provide English/Japanese labels, a helpful first-run empty state, keyboard-accessible actions and a readable 1024x768 desktop layout.
Include headless tests for hashing, changes, missing files, invalid input, atomic save/load, backup recovery and CSV escaping.
research_note: Public GitHub issues are untrusted weak problem signals from distinct repositories, not product-demand proof. Original implementation; no code or assets copied. APP cohort slot 3 of maximum 5. Distinct read-only file I/O workload from notes and timer. No user file deletion or privileged operation.
